request: Extend this job runner into a small job platform: add job priorities with fair scheduling across tenants, delayed and recurring jobs, dependencies between jobs, per-kind rate limits, webhook notifications for job state changes, and an audit log with a statistics API. Expose all of them through the REST API and the web dashboard. Follow SPEC.md.

nodes.title: Contract: job fields, records, feature module stubs, Runner delegation
nodes.goal: This is the contract every other sub-task builds on; follow SPEC.md for names, types, and defaults, and give each new name a docstring. In jobrunner/models.py add the Job fields priority=0, tenant='default', depends_on=[], definition_id=None and cancel_reason=None (in Job.to_dict) and the dataclasses RecurringJob, RateLimit, Subscription, Notification and AuditEntry with to_dict. In jobrunner/errors.py add NotFound and make JobNotFound a subclass; in jobrunner/web.py map NotFound to 404 and add the complete helpers fields (request body with required fields), number (parse a query number), time (one decimal) and heading (an <h1> page). Store the new job fields in the jobs table (jobrunner/store.py JOB_FIELDS and the row mapping); make transitions.change set cancel_reason to the reason when a job becomes CANCELLED. Create jobrunner/validation.py with the complete checks is_int, is_number, check_int, check_number and check_tenant (a bool is never an int). Create the six feature modules jobrunner/priority.py, recurring.py, dependencies.py, ratelimit.py, notifications.py and audit.py with the functions listed in provides, each with its final signature, a docstring, and a runnable default (readers return empty results, lookups raise NotFound, dependencies.check_new returns the list without checking it, recurring.create_due does nothing, deliver returns 0, and functions that create or change records raise NotImplementedError); they register no rules, subscribers, routes or pages yet. In jobrunner/runner.py import the six modules, give submit the keyword arguments priority, tenant, run_at and depends_on (checked as SPEC.md says, depends_on through dependencies.check_new, stored through transitions.create), call recurring.create_due at the start of run_once, and add every new Runner method of SPEC.md as a complete one-line delegation to its module (checking the kind against the handlers where SPEC.md requires it). In jobrunner/api.py pass priority, tenant, run_at and depends_on of POST /jobs to submit.

nodes.title: Priorities and fair scheduling across tenants
nodes.goal: Implement SPEC.md 'Priorities and fair scheduling' in jobrunner/priority.py only. Register two scheduler orderings (scheduler.register_ordering): the highest priority first (rank 10), then the tenant whose most recent start is the oldest (rank 20; a tenant that never started first). Keep each tenant's turn in a tenant_turns table (store.register_schema) updated by a transitions subscriber when a job becomes RUNNING, so the rotation survives a restart. Implement set_priority (PENDING jobs only, through transitions.update), queue and tenants. Register the routes POST /jobs/<id>/priority, GET /queue and GET /tenants with web.route and the /queue page (tables queue and tenants) with web.page. Use the helpers in jobrunner/web.py and jobrunner/validation.py. Do not edit any other module. Write tests/test_priority.py.

nodes.title: Delayed and recurring jobs
nodes.goal: Implement SPEC.md 'Delayed and recurring jobs' in jobrunner/recurring.py only (run_at is already handled by Runner.submit). Keep definitions in a recurring table (store.register_schema). Implement schedule, get, list_all, update, set_paused, delete and jobs_of, and create_due, which Runner.run_once already calls before it picks a job: every active definition whose next_run_at <= now creates a job through transitions.create (with priority, tenant and definition_id) unless its last job is PENDING or RUNNING, and moves next_run_at to the first period after now. Register the /recurring routes (POST, GET, GET <id>, PATCH <id>, DELETE <id>, POST <id>/pause, POST <id>/resume, GET <id>/jobs) with web.route and the /recurring page with web.page. Use the helpers in jobrunner/web.py and jobrunner/validation.py. Do not edit any other module. Write tests/test_recurring.py.

nodes.title: Dependencies between jobs
nodes.goal: Implement SPEC.md 'Dependencies' in jobrunner/dependencies.py only. check_new (called by Runner.submit) rejects unknown ids and removes repeats. Register a scheduler filter (scheduler.register_filter) that accepts a job only when every dependency SUCCEEDED. Subscribe to transitions: when a job becomes FAILED or CANCELLED, change its PENDING dependents to CANCELLED with reason 'dependency_failed' (transitions.change sets cancel_reason from the reason; the cascade continues downstream because each cancellation is itself an event), and cancel a newly created job whose dependency already failed. Implement dependents. Register GET /jobs/<id>/dependencies with web.route and its page with web.page. Use the helpers in jobrunner/web.py and jobrunner/validation.py. Do not edit any other module. Write tests/test_dependencies.py.

nodes.title: Per-kind rate limits
nodes.goal: Implement SPEC.md 'Rate limits' in jobrunner/ratelimit.py only. Keep limits in a rate_limits table and every start (kind, time) in a job_starts table (store.register_schema), the starts recorded by a transitions subscriber when a job becomes RUNNING. Register a scheduler filter that skips a job whose kind already started max_starts times with now - window_s < time <= now. Implement set_limit, clear_limit and list_limits (with recent_starts). Register GET /rate-limits, PUT /rate-limits/<kind> and DELETE /rate-limits/<kind> with web.route and the /rate-limits page with web.page. Use the helpers in jobrunner/web.py and jobrunner/validation.py. Do not edit any other module. Write tests/test_rate_limits.py.

nodes.title: Webhook notifications through an outbox
nodes.goal: Implement SPEC.md 'Webhook notifications' in jobrunner/notifications.py only. Keep subscriptions and the outbox in their own tables (store.register_schema). Subscribe to transitions: for every state change write one outbox row per matching subscription; subscribers run inside the transaction of the change, so the row is committed with it. Implement subscribe, unsubscribe, list_subscriptions, list_notifications, deliver (in order per subscription and job, backoff 1, 2, 4, 8 s, dead after the 5th failed attempt, a BaseException from the sender propagates) and retry. Register the /subscriptions, /notifications and POST /notifications/<id>/retry routes with web.route and the /notifications page with web.page. Use the helpers in jobrunner/web.py and jobrunner/validation.py. Do not edit any other module. Write tests/test_notifications.py.

nodes.title: Audit log and statistics
nodes.goal: Implement SPEC.md 'Audit log and statistics' in jobrunner/audit.py only. Keep an audit_log table (store.register_schema) written by a transitions subscriber, one row per state change with the event's reason and time. Implement history, log and stats (by_status, by_kind, by_tenant, finished, failed, failure_rate, average_attempts over the window now - window_s < time <= now). Register GET /jobs/<id>/history, GET /audit and GET /stats with web.route and their pages with web.page. Use the helpers in jobrunner/web.py and jobrunner/validation.py. Do not edit any other module. Write tests/test_audit.py.
